_comment: The entries to submit to SchemaStore (schemastore/schemastore → src/api/json/catalog.json),
kept here so the patterns we register are reviewable and versioned alongside the schemas.
Once accepted, every editor that consults SchemaStore — VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim — gets
completion, hover docs and validation with no configuration at all.
fileMatch is the *file type*, not one filename: Draugr loads any path you hand it, so a repo
can hold azure.saga.yaml, draugr-api.saga.yaml, or a bare .saga.yaml. draugr.saga.yaml is
only the name `draugr init` writes by default.
The two file types are deliberately distinguishable. The Saga schema requires `release`, so a
fragment named *.saga.yaml would be matched by the Saga entry and reported as invalid in
every editor that reads this catalogue — permanently, with no fix available to the user.
*.saga-fragment.yaml does not match *.saga.yaml, which is the point of the suffix.
Submit only once each schema is served from draugr.dev. A catalogue entry is a URL and
editors cache the catalogue, so registering ahead of publication hands out a 404 that gets
fixed on their refresh schedule rather than ours.
